content.title: About
content.content: Heavy cream is a dairy product with a high fat content (typically 35‑40 %). It is obtained by separating the cream from whole milk and is used in cooking to make sauces, desserts, whipped toppings, and to add a rich, creamy texture to dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Heavy cream is often called “whipping cream” because of its ability to hold air when whipped.
In the United States, cream with at least 36 % fat is classified as heavy cream, while in Europe it is similar to “double cream.”
Cream can be pasteurized or ultra‑pasteurized; the latter extends shelf life.
When whipped, the fat forms a stable emulsion that creates a firm, airy foam.
Heavy cream is a key ingredient in classic sauces such as Hollandaise and desserts like crème brûlée.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Heavy cream provides vitamin A, which supports vision and immune function.

items.title: Contains fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: Vitamins D, E and K are present in cream, contributing to bone health, antioxidant protection, and blood clotting.

items.title: Energy‑dense
items.content: The high fat content offers a quick source of energy.

items.title: Aids nutrient absorption
items.content: The fats in cream help absorb other fat‑soluble nutrients and carotenoids from meals.

items.title: Improves taste and texture
items.content: Cream adds a smooth mouthfeel and rich flavor, enhancing the palatability of many dishes.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Heavy cream is calorie‑dense; excessive intake may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: A large proportion of saturated fat can affect cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream contains lactose, making it unsuitable for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins found in cream.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heavy cream is used for whipping, making sauces, soups, desserts (mousses, custards) and in baking. It can be added to coffee for a silky texture or used as a base for butter‑based sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cream in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in its original container or a sealed jar. After opening, use within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or off‑color.

infant-formula-premature-powder-made-wit.title: Infant formula, premature, powder, made with water

content.title: About
content.content: Premature infant formula is a specially designed nutritional powder for newborns born before term. It provides an optimal balance of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals needed for the growth and development of a preterm baby. Preparation is simple: just add clean water.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Enriched with DHA and ARA – essential fatty acids important for brain and eye development.
Contains prebiotics that support healthy gut microbiota.
Formulated to meet the higher protein and energy needs of premature infants.
Packaging is calculated for a 30‑day course when fed according to pediatric guidelines.
The formula has undergone clinical testing and is approved by pediatric associations.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: A balanced mix of protein, fat, and carbohydrate supplies the energy and building blocks needed for rapid growth in preterm infants.

items.title: Brain and eye development
items.content: DHA and ARA promote neuronal connections and visual system maturation during this critical period.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc help maintain the infant’s defensive mechanisms.

items.title: Healthy gut flora
items.content: Prebiotics such as GOS stimulate beneficial bacteria, reducing the risk of infections.

items.title: Optimal electrolyte balance
items.content: The formula provides sodium, potassium, and chloride in ratios suited to premature babies’ needs.

items.title: Cow‑milk protein allergy
items.content: Some infants may develop an allergic reaction; if rash, vomiting, or diarrhea appear, stop use and consult a physician.

items.title: Preparation accuracy
items.content: Incorrect water‑to‑powder ratio can cause hypo‑ or hyper‑osmolarity, which is dangerous for the baby.

items.title: Shelf life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the powder should be used within 48 hours and kept refrigerated.

items.title: Water temperature control
items.content: Water should be warm (~37 °C); water that is too hot or too cold impairs solubility and may harm the infant’s digestive system.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Measure the recommended amount of powder (usually one level scoop) and add it to pre‑warmed clean water, stirring thoroughly until fully dissolved. Allow the mixture to cool to body temperature before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and use within 48 hours. Discard the formula if it develops an off‑smell, color change, or unusual taste.

content.title: About
content.content: A jelly sandwich is a classic sweet snack made of two slices of soft white bread with fruit jelly spread between them. Common flavors include strawberry, raspberry or orange jelly. The sandwich is popular in the US and the UK as a quick bite or a children’s treat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded jelly‑sandwich recipe appeared in cookbooks of the early 20th century.
In the 1950s American school cafeterias often served jelly sandwiches as a standard lunch item.
There is an “upside‑down” version where the jelly is placed on top of the bread and covered with cream cheese.
In Japan a popular variant uses matcha (green tea) jelly on white bread.
The sandwich can be wrapped in plastic film, making it a favorite for picnics.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Fruit jelly provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many desserts, a jelly sandwich contains little fat when made with lean bread.

items.title: Carbohydrates for energy
items.content: The sugars in the jelly give a quick energy boost, useful before physical activity.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Fruit jelly contains water, contributing modestly to hydration.

items.title: Psychological comfort
items.content: The nostalgic taste often improves mood and reduces stress.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High amounts of sugar in jelly can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Artificial colour allergens
items.content: Some commercial jellies contain synthetic colourings that may trigger allergies.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: Traditional white bread contains gluten, which is problematic for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Fruit acids can irritate a sensitive stomach if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich chilled or at room temperature. Cut it into small squares for kids or triangles for adults. You can add cream cheese, nut butter or fresh berries for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep a prepared jelly sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours to prevent the bread from drying out and the jelly from losing its shape. For longer storage, keep the jelly and bread separate.

content.title: About
content.content: The Quarter Pounder is a classic McDonald's burger featuring a 113 g (¼‑lb) beef patty, American cheese, onions, pickles, ketchup and mustard, served on a sesame‑seed bun.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The burger was introduced to the U.S. menu in 1971 and quickly became a staple.
The name reflects the patty’s weight – a quarter of a pound (≈ 113 g).
In some markets, such as Japan, a double‑patty version called the “Double Quarter Pounder” is offered.
Since the 2020s McDonald's has offered a “Quarter Pounder with Cheese” without onions and pickles upon customer request.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The beef patty provides about 20 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is readily absorbed.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc aids immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: American cheese adds calcium for bone health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of protein, fat and carbs offers a quick energy boost.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: One Quarter Pounder contains roughly 520 kcal, so it should be accounted for in daily intake.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: The patty and cheese contribute saturated fat and salt, which can affect cholesterol and blood pressure.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The sesame bun contains gluten, important for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: American cheese may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The burger is served hot. It can be customized with extra sauces, added bacon, or a gluten‑free bun upon request.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burger in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze it and reheat in a microwave or oven before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: Veggie burger patty, no bun is a ready‑to‑cook plant‑based patty designed as a meat‑free alternative to traditional burger patties. It typically contains pea protein, vegetable fibers, spices and plant oils, delivering a taste, texture and nutritional profile similar to a conventional beef burger.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The patty provides about 15 g of plant protein per 100 g.
Pea protein is a complete protein, containing all essential amino acids.
The product is gluten‑free when no wheat‑based additives are used.
Many versions are fortified with iron and vitamin B12 to offset possible deficiencies in vegan diets.
When cooked properly, the patty stays juicy with a crisp exterior, mimicking a meat patty.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Plant protein supports muscle growth and repair, especially important for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Most fats are poly‑ and monounsaturated, which are heart‑healthy.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetable fibers aid digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are essential for immune function and metabolism; they are often added during fortification.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: Plant‑based foods contain no cholesterol, making them suitable for cholesterol‑lowering diets.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pea protein.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: To enhance flavor, the patty may contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Processed ingredients
items.content: Certain versions may include preservatives or flavor enhancers; choose products with short ingredient lists.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Eating large amounts of processed plant patties could lead to micronutrient imbalances if the overall diet lacks variety.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The patty can be pan‑fried, baked, or grilled. Cook until a golden crust forms, about 3–4 minutes per side. Serve with vegetables, sauces, leafy greens, or in a whole‑grain bun.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–4 °C in the original packaging or an airtight container for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Discard if any off‑smell or mold appears.
